lines.text: Sixty thousand people out there. They have been waiting for you all day.
Your bag. I counted them twice. They're all there.
Even the one with no name on it.
Go on. You know why.
NINE YEARS EARLIER
You've been at that listening station for an hour. I close in ten minutes.
So you mix. On a laptop. With the sync button. Mm.
Sync is training wheels, kid. One day you take them off.
Here. White label. No name, no artist, nothing.
Play it when you know why.
This is it? A plastic controller with a sync button? Fine. Make them dance, superstar.
Ignore him. One more trick, and Saturday we show him.
Two desk lamps, one bedsheet, and a red sock. Behold: the light show!
Doors are open. Well, the door. Six people. Your night. Go.
02:14. MUM BANGS ON THE WALL.
NEXT SATURDAY: SOMEBODY'S GARAGE.
END OF CHAPTER 1
You're the DJ? Good. I'm Sara. I'll be right there, in front. Don't make me stop.
That's Sara. She dances to anything. Don't test it.
03:40. THE NEIGHBOURS CALL THE POLICE.
THE POLICE STAY FOR ONE MORE RECORD.
END OF CHAPTER 2
So you're Lia's new kid. No sync, she says. Saturday I'll be listening. Every join.
Don't mind him. He's been coming in every Saturday for thirty years. He's never bought anything.
18:00. LIA HANDS YOU A KEY.
THURSDAYS, THE SHOP IS YOURS.
END OF CHAPTER 3
Tuesdays, nine till one. No money, but exposure. Lots of exposure. Don't scare the regulars.
Exposure. Great. We'll eat exposure.
01:00. RUI PAYS YOU IN FREE DRINKS.
A WOMAN AT THE BAR ASKS FOR YOUR NUMBER. SHE RUNS A RADIO SHOW.
END OF CHAPTER 4
Thursday, eleven to midnight. Live. Dead air is a sin. And the news starts on the hour. Not a second late.
On the hour. No pressure, then.
VERA: SAME TIME NEXT WEEK.
1,204 LISTENERS. YOUR MUM WAS ONE OF THEM.
END OF CHAPTER 5
Not on the list.
We're the warm-up! CAVE called us after the radio show! Look again!
Warm-up. Downstairs. Mind the step.
02:00. HELENA VOSS ARRIVES. SHE HEARD YOUR LAST RECORD FROM THE STAIRS.
ON THE WAY OUT, NUNO HOLDS THE DOOR: "NEXT TIME, YOU'RE ON THE LIST."
END OF CHAPTER 6
You warmed up for me like you meant it. Nobody does that any more. Fridays, peak time. They're yours.
Fridays. At CAVE. Peak time. Somebody pinch me.
All yours, superstar. Two hours, every second planned. Try that some time.
He pressed play two hours ago and went to the bar. Go and show them what a DJ does.
06:30. THE LIGHTS COME ON. NOBODY WANTS TO GO HOME.
VEX POSTS A PHOTO OF YOUR CROWD. CAPTION: "MY PEOPLE."
END OF CHAPTER 7
MONDAY. THE LABEL WRITES BACK: "NOT FOR US."
FRIDAY. HELENA PLAYS YOUR DUBPLATE AT HER SET ANYWAY.
END OF CHAPTER 8
So you're the kid from Lisbon. Helena says you can play anything, on anything. My booth is tired. Show me.
Tired. The left fader is dead, and one of the turntables has had a long night.
IBIZA AIRPORT. YOUR RECORD BAG WENT TO MÁLAGA.
JOLI LENDS YOU HERS. YOU KNOW NONE OF THESE RECORDS.
DETROIT. A RECORD SHOP ON A STREET WITH NO OTHER SHOPS.
THE OWNER PLAYS YOU A TEST PRESSING FROM 1991 AND WATCHES YOUR FACE.
THAT NIGHT YOU PLAY YOUR FORTIETH SET IN FORTY DAYS.
LISBON. GROOVELINE RECORDS. LIA PUTS ON A RECORD AND SAYS NOTHING FOR AN HOUR.
THEN: "WHY DO YOU PLAY, KID?"
END OF CHAPTER 9
I'm Carla. I manage people who get booked. Three festivals this summer: a tent, a forest, and a sunset slot. Don't be late.
A manager. We have a manager. Mum is going to love this.
FESTIVAL TWO. YOUR SLOT IS 3 PM.
TWO HUNDRED PEOPLE ON A FIELD MADE FOR TWENTY THOUSAND.
01:00. THE TREES ARE STILL SHAKING.
CARLA ON THE PHONE: "HELENA VOSS WANTS YOU. BACK TO BACK. NEXT MONTH."
END OF CHAPTER 10
Back to back. One booth, two DJs. I play a record, you answer it. And you never touch my deck.
Helena Voss. In the same booth as me. Don't touch her deck. Got it.
19:30. AN OLD BOAT ON THE TEJO, THE BRIDGE IN THE SUNSET.
ONE BOOTH, TWO DECKS. THE LEFT ONE IS HELENA'S.
Back to back, superstar. My laptop, your little records. Try to keep up.
His name on top of the poster, yours underneath. Smaller. Just play your records.
06:30. HIS LAPTOP IS STILL ON THE MIXER. BLACK.
DANI, AT THE BAR, NO SUNGLASSES: "TEACH ME. THE RECORDS, I MEAN."
END OF CHAPTER 11
MERIDIAN called. The closing set, on the main stage. Sixty thousand people. They asked for you by name.
MERIDIAN. The closing set. Nine years ago it was a lamp, a bedsheet and Mira. Somebody pinch me.
THE NIGHT BEFORE MERIDIAN.
YOUR OLD ROOM. THE SAME LAMP, THE SAME BEDSHEET. EVERYONE CAME.
PLAY THEM YOUR CLOSING SET. ONCE.
